hook: NASA's Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory, a space telescope, ended its 22-year mission after a failed rescue.

sections.voiceover: NASA's Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory, a space telescope, ended its 22-year mission after a failed rescue.
sections.visual_cue: Graphic showing the Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory in orbit.
b_roll: NASA illustration of Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory

sections.voiceover: On October 20, 2026, NASA officially concluded the science mission of the Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory. Could a commercial spacecraft save it?
sections.visual_cue: Map showing satellite altitude relative to Earth.
b_roll: NASA diagram of low Earth orbit

sections.voiceover: Arizona's Katalyst Space Technologies tried to save the observatory, but their LINK spacecraft failed the mission.
sections.visual_cue: Logo of Katalyst Space Technologies on screen.

sections.voiceover: The LINK spacecraft failed to reach the Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory during the summer of 2026. This mission leaves behind 22 years of data from visible, ultraviolet, X-ray, and gamma-ray telescopes.
sections.visual_cue: Animation of the failed docking maneuver.

sections.voiceover: NASA permanently shut down the Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory in October 2026 after the failed rescue.
sections.visual_cue: Slow zoom out to the stars.
b_roll: Public domain footage of deep space
